move: canvas text wipes in under RGB-split slice tears, settles, tears out again
how: A full-frame 2D canvas redrawn every frame from an offscreen text mask ('SYSTEM ONLINE' plus a mint spaced subline). A reveal value wipes the mask in from the left with expo.out over the first 30%, holds fully visible until 78%, then wipes back out with expo.in. A glitch intensity envelope is hard during the reveal (decaying 1 to 0), near zero while settled with occasional sine-timed hiccups, and ramps back to 1 for the exit. Each frame, with a per-frame seeded rng, the frame is cut into 6 to 28 horizontal slices that shift up to 140px, some rows dropped, each slice drawn as red and cyan tinted copies offset by up to 18px in 'lighter' blend under the clean copy; up to 30 mint/white noise chips scatter, faint scanlines step every 4px, and a soft mint scan bar sweeps top to bottom once per loop. The canvas ends empty with the bar back at the top, so it loops visually.
adapt: Change the two strings, the font, the accent colour used for chips/subline/bar, and the ink/paper colours; the intensity envelope breakpoints (0.9s, 2.1s, 2.35s) scale with D. Keep the per-frame seeded rng so renders are deterministic and the slice/split amplitudes.
port: mount(el, shot) appends a canvas sized to the shot and two offscreen canvases, preloads the font via document.fonts.load, and pre-renders the text mask; animate(el, shot, D) returns a gsap.timeline with one proxy tween {t: 0 to D, ease 'none'} whose onUpdate runs the seek(t) drawing code. gsap.parseEase is used for the reveal curves; no document-level selectors beyond the canvas, but W/H must come from the canvas, not constants.
caveats: fx.register canvas seek loop must become an onUpdate tween on the returned timeline
redraws the full 1280x720 canvas up to 3 times per slice each frame; moderately slow
the canvas is a fixed 1280x720 backing store scaled by CSS
needs the font loaded before the first frame or the mask is drawn in a fallback face
